---

I scanned the spec against the full ambiguity taxonomy. It is unusually complete — functional scope, failure handling, exit statuses, and terminology are all Clear. I found 5 unresolved points that would change test assertions or implementation, all clustered in **byte-exact output** and **input tolerance**. Starting with the highest-impact one.

**Question:** When the web-page export contains a title with a single quote or an apostrophe, must the output escape exactly the characters FR-014 names (`&`, `<`, `>`, plus `"` inside the link address) and leave everything else literal, or is any escaping that keeps the page well-formed acceptable?

Why it matters: FR-012 says the page must be "exactly this form", but FR-014 says escaping covers those characters "at minimum". If "at minimum" stands, two correct implementations can emit different bytes for the same bookmark, and no test can assert the output exactly — which is how every other output format in this project is tested.

**Recommended:** Option A - The rest of the spec pins output to the byte (`001:FR-019a`, `001:FR-020a`, FR-013), and a closed escaping set is the only version of FR-014 that is testable by exact comparison; it also keeps apostrophes in titles readable in the page source.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Exactly those four, and no others: `&`→`&`, `<`→`<`, `>`→`>` in address, title and labels, plus `"`→`"` in the `href` value only. Every other character, including `'`, is emitted literally. |
| B | Same four, plus `'`→`'` everywhere (what Python's default HTML-escaping helper produces), fixed as the required bytes. |
| C | Leave it open: any escaping is acceptable as long as a standard page reader recovers the stored address and title (tests parse the page instead of comparing bytes). |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (<=5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
